comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence (Kunstmatige Intelligentie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 degree combines a 135 EC major with 45 EC of profiling space. The example follows Learning and Computation, one of three 45 EC depth packages, and illustrates one course from each required choice group. It includes 7.5 EC of experimental methods before the 7.5 EC thesis. With approval, students can write a 15 EC thesis using another 7.5 EC from the profiling space.
components: Utrecht requires a supervised thesis after preparation in experimental methods. UCR offers optional independent research outside these schedules.
Utrecht leaves 45 EC for profiling, such as a minor or electives, subject to programme requirements.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized Kunstmatige Intelligentie target does not select among Utrecht’s three formal 45-EC depth packages. The adopted 2026–2027 OER lists Learning and Computation first, so it is instantiated by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. Bound choices B and C are represented by the first listed eligible course in each official choice group; the 45-EC profiling space remains open because the OER does not prescribe one subject.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Artificial intelligence, intelligent agents and computational models
Programming, algorithms, software and computer systems
Mathematics, logic, probability, statistics and formal modelling
Machine learning, neural networks, deep learning and reinforcement learning
Cognition, psychology, neuroscience, perception and learning
Decision-making, optimisation and intelligent autonomous systems
Ethics, philosophy and responsible artificial intelligence
Experimental design, research methods, academic communication and independent research
adjacent: Cognitive processing and computational models of mind
questions: How can intelligent systems learn, reason, decide and act?
What can computational models reveal about human thought, perception and language?
How should AI systems be designed and evaluated responsibly?

alternatives.label: Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Science
alternatives.concept: Study machine learning and intelligent systems alongside human perception, language and cognition. Build programming, mathematics and experimental skills, and use them to explore how machines and people learn and make decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: Study machine learning and intelligent systems alongside human perception, language and cognition. Build programming, mathematics and experimental skills, and use them to explore how machines and people learn and make decisions.
progression: Programming and mathematics precede software development, robotics and advanced AI. Introductory brain and behaviour precedes the available spring Psycholinguistics course, then neurobiology and the gateway underpin later cognition. Machine learning precedes deep learning.

alternatives.label: Machine Learning, Software and Autonomous Systems
alternatives.concept: Build models and software for systems that learn, see and act. Develop skills in algorithms, robotics, vision and reinforcement learning, and study how AI is used and governed in business.
alternatives.labelReason: Build models and software for systems that learn, see and act. Develop skills in algorithms, robotics, vision and reinforcement learning, and study how AI is used and governed in business.
alternatives.distinctness: The software and autonomous-systems plan adds databases, operating systems, advanced algorithms, numerical methods and reinforcement learning. It focuses on building and testing computational systems rather than developing a sequence in human cognition.
progression: Programming, data and mathematics precede advanced algorithms and robotics. Probability and linear algebra precede advanced learning, with machine learning before neural networks and reinforcement learning.

alternatives.label: AI, Reasoning and Human Cognition
alternatives.concept: Study computational reasoning alongside the science and philosophy of mind. Use logic, algorithms and AI models to examine intelligence, and study human perception, language, social cognition and evidence from behavioural research.
alternatives.labelReason: Study computational reasoning alongside the science and philosophy of mind. Use logic, algorithms and AI models to examine intelligence, and study human perception, language, social cognition and evidence from behavioural research.
alternatives.distinctness: The human cognition plan adds social and developmental psychology, research synthesis and philosophy of mind and agency. These courses support questions about reasoning and human intelligence, alongside foundational formal logic, algorithms and AI.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes the available spring Psycholinguistics course and higher cognition. Introductory philosophy precedes philosophy of mind and agency. Experimental statistics precedes research synthesis, and machine learning precedes deep learning.

selection.assessment: The closest option integrates computational AI with cognitive science. The learning and computation direction develops software, advanced algorithms and autonomous systems. The reasoning and computation direction develops formal logic and algorithmic thinking alongside human cognition and philosophy, with limited advanced symbolic AI. Cognitive Processing also has direct support in UCR perception, cognition and language courses. These contribute to the closest and human-cognition options. The comparison presents three options.

blocks: Both develop programming and computational problem-solving. UCR uses Python.
Both study methods for intelligent systems. UCR focuses on probabilistic decision-making under uncertainty.
Both study data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
Both teach machine-learning methods and model evaluation. UCR covers regression, classification and unsupervised learning.
UCR studies transformers and language applications within a broader neural networks course. Utrecht provides a dedicated language models course.
UCR develops advanced learning through reinforcement learning and implementing agents. Utrecht’s course covers a broader set of advanced machine-learning methods.
Both teach mathematics for modelling. UCR focuses on calculus, equations and dynamic models.
Both develop formal logic for computing and AI. UCR also covers discrete structures and proof techniques.
Both develop statistical and experimental methods for empirical research.
Both introduce human cognition and ways to study it. UCR also gives an introduction to neuroanatomy and behaviour.
Both study language processing and how to investigate it. UCR emphasises the psychology and neuroscience of language.
Utrecht builds computational models of language processing. UCR studies language applications within deep learning and human language in psycholinguistics.
Both consider philosophical questions about intelligence and mind. UCR also studies identity and conscious experience.
Both consider philosophical questions about AI. UCR focuses on issues such as fairness, privacy, agency and responsibility.
Utrecht provides a dedicated course on formal and natural languages. UCR covers related formal tools within logic and algorithms.
Utrecht devotes a course to connections between natural processes and computation.
Utrecht provides a dedicated advanced logic course. UCR develops formal reasoning within logic and algorithms.
Utrecht requires a supervised thesis after preparation in experimental methods. UCR offers optional independent research outside these schedules.
Utrecht leaves 45 EC for profiling, such as a minor or electives, subject to programme requirements.

notes.text: Utrecht combines a common AI core with a formal depth package. UCR covers related topics across AI, mathematics, software, cognitive science and philosophy. Utrecht gives more dedicated study to formal languages, advanced logic and computational language processing.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Artificial Intelligence bachelor studies intelligence in people and machines through computing, mathematics, cognitive science, language and philosophy.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The 2026–2027 example follows Utrecht’s Learning and Computation package. The three UCR plans focus on AI and cognitive science, software and autonomous systems, or reasoning and human cognition.
